title: Catalogue against order lines
prompt: The catalogue team is checking products against what was sold. Write `solve(products, order_items)` so it returns `product_id`, `name`, `order_id` and `line_no` for every product and every order line, matched where they can be.
rules: A product with order lines appears once per line. A product that was never sold appears once, with `order_id` and `line_no` missing.
An order line whose product isn't in `products` still appears, with `name` missing.
`product_id` is always filled in, from whichever side has it. Return only these four columns, in this order.
hints: Nothing may be dropped from either side. Which join type keeps every row of both?
With `on="product_id"`, Spark keeps one `product_id` column and fills it from whichever side matched.
Join first, then `select` the four columns.
